rationale: ary3 is a tight floating-point loop kernel ( Shootout matrix multiply) where the entire program is a single 474-byte main dominated by inner-loop arithmetic; any per-iteration control-flow overhead directly destroys its runtime. BCF and FLA are therefore omitted entirely, since opaque-predicate checks on every basic block and dispatcher-based flattening are exactly the transformations that wreck hot-loop performance, and the tiny 512-byte text section leaves no room for their code bloat. The retained passes are all low-cost, correctness-safe local transforms: SUB (instruction substitution) diversifies the FP/integer arithmetic without changing loop iteration counts, SPLIT breaks up the loop body cheaply, and IBR/ICALL/IGV add modest indirection with weights tuned so the high RuntimeCost (0.8-0.9) and CorrectnessRisk (0.7-0.8) dimensions dominate the selection, ensuring these passes are applied only to cold regions or omitted when features indicate hot-loop code, while moderate SecurityGain/DiversityGain (0.4-0.6) values still reward them where features favor those dimensions.
